clue.text: Place where spinners will take a turn

indicators.note: turning round here means the word for spinners is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: tops are toys that spin

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch where spin bowlers come on to bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests spin bowlers getting their over; the spinners are really toy tops.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular location, a synonym of place.

clue.text: Settled without recourse to law

parts.note: people who occupy empty property without any legal right have settled there unlawfully

explanation.surface: A dispute resolved out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled without recourse to law' reads as an out-of-court agreement, but it means set up home somewhere with no legal title.
explanation.definitionFit: Squatters occupy property and live there without any lawful entitlement.

clue.text: Their quarters are combed for food

definitions.text: Their quarters are combed for food

parts.words: Their quarters are combed for food
parts.note: a hive's honeycomb is both the insects' living quarters and the source of honey that people harvest

explanation.surface: Someone's lodgings being searched for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combed' looks like 'searched' but refers to honeycomb, where these insects live and store honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeybees live in hives built of wax honeycomb, from which honey is taken.

clue.text: Criminal purpose in proposal

indicators.note: in places the word for purpose inside the word for proposal

parts.note: an offer is a proposal
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker's intent, hidden within an offer or suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker is someone who has committed a crime, a synonym for a criminal.

clue.text: Opening bottle before the game, get drunk

indicators.note: before puts the bottle's letter ahead of the game in a down entry
the opening of a word is its first letter, here of bottle

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: Cracking open a bottle before the match and getting drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal slang for extremely intoxicated.

clue.text: Offer nothing but gentle affection

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid
love means a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Giving nothing except soft-hearted fondness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means gentle and love is affection, so the phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Contempt, when party leader's on platform

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
a word's leader is its first letter, here of party

parts.note: odium is hatred or contempt

explanation.surface: Scorn as a political party's leader takes the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' looks like a politician but just gives P, the first letter of party.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised stand that a speaker or winner stands on, a kind of platform.

clue.text: Boy naturally opposed to the current trend

definitions.meaning: Eddie or ... is a boy's name

definitions.text: naturally opposed to the current trend
definitions.meaning: a whirl of water turns against the main flow of the stream as a matter of course

explanation.surface: A contrary lad who instinctively bucks the fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current trend' sounds like fashion; it is a flowing stream, and a swirl runs counter to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, and a small whirlpool where water circles back against the flow.

clue.text: Resentment at card game not finishing

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter of the card game is dropped

parts.note: piquet is a two-player card game

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a game of cards left uncompleted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or wounded pride, close to resentment.

clue.text: Treacherous outlaw in fiction

parts.note: false means disloyal or treacherous
Robin Hood is the outlaw of English legend

explanation.surface: A disloyal bandit who appears in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fiction' suggests Robin Hood's legend, but fiction is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untruth, something made up, as fiction is.

clue.text: Short-termer that's escaped is put back under canvas

indicators.note: being under canvas means camping, so these letters go inside the tent

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
ran means fled or escaped

indicators.note: put back means the word is is reversed

explanation.surface: A temporary inmate who fled and was then returned to camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' is the idiom for camping, so it signals going inside a tent; 'put back' reverses the word 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transient is someone who stays only briefly, such as a temporary lodger or worker.

clue.text: Female subject of an old song cycle

definitions.text: Female subject of an old song cycle

parts.words: Female subject of an old song cycle
parts.note: the music-hall song '... Bell' is about a woman courted on a bicycle built for two

explanation.surface: A woman celebrated in a classical cycle of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song cycle' suggests a classical set of songs; the cycle is the bicycle in the 1892 song 'Daisy Bell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy is the woman addressed in the old popular song about a tandem bicycle.

clue.text: Revised tale with revolutionary ending

indicators.note: with joins the second piece to the end of the first
revised means reworked, so the letters of tale are rearranged

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary or communist

explanation.surface: A story rewritten so it ends in revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' does double duty, as definition and as the anagram signal on TALE, giving ALTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something altered has been changed, as a revised version has.

clue.text: Man, after a kiss, accepted proposition

indicators.note: after places Man following the a and the kiss

parts.note: X is the cross used to mean a kiss
IOM stands for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A fellow who, following a kiss, accepted a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement taken as self-evidently true, a proposition accepted without proof.

clue.text: All those looking at papers for university post

definitions.meaning: the total audience of a newspaper is everyone who reads it
a reader is a senior academic rank in British universities, just below professor

explanation.surface: Everyone reading the newspapers for a job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a Reader is a senior lecturer post, so the office held is a readership.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper's audience of readers, and the position of a university Reader.

clue.text: Some ran badly, running not being their sport

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of some ran are put in a poor new order

explanation.surface: Several athletes ran poorly because running is not their event.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers compete in boats, so their sport is rowing rather than racing on foot.

clue.text: Hose in New York left running

parts.note: on means operating or running, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Stockings left to run in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a garden pipe but means stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, and hose is an old word for stockings.

clue.text: Country taking in reciprocal aid

indicators.note: reciprocal suggests going back the other way, so the word aid is read backwards

explanation.surface: A nation receiving aid in an exchange arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Removed, as I'm in the way

indicators.note: in puts the first-person letter inside the abbreviation for road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the speaker gives the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave because they are an obstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammar is loose: 'I'm' has to stand for I, which goes into RD.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rid of something is to have it removed or got rid of.

clue.text: Act, taking a central role, then quit

indicators.note: taking a central means the act takes the role right into its middle

parts.note: a deed is an act
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An actor who played the lead and then walked off.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means left or went away, as one who has quit.

clue.text: Refuse of autumn left out

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is taken away from the season

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Leaves remaining as the debris of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the waste parts of a butchered animal, and so rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: Appropriate point to consider when renting premises

parts.note: fitting means suitable or appropriate
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A relevant issue to think about when leasing a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Fixtures and fittings are listed in property lets, so they are things to consider.
explanation.definitionFit: Fittings are removable items in a property, a standard matter in a lease or rental.

clue.text: Wrong way to give people a hand

definitions.text: Wrong way to give people a hand

parts.words: Wrong way to give people a hand
parts.note: a hand is a set of cards, so giving out cards incorrectly is the wrong way to provide them

explanation.surface: The improper method of helping others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give people a hand' suggests helping; at cards it means distributing a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeal is a faulty distribution of playing cards to the players.

clue.text: Fights waste

definitions.meaning: leftover bits of food or material thrown away

explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are both minor brawls and discarded leftovers.

clue.text: Defeat looks far from good in the record

indicators.note: in puts the wrongdoing inside the record

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
sin is wrongdoing, far from good

explanation.surface: A loss looks bad when written into the history books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks' is a link word meaning the defeat appears as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing, as a noun, is the experience of being beaten, a defeat.

clue.text: Quickly takes direction for the city

parts.note: presto is the musical term meaning quickly
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone swiftly getting directions to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston is a city in Lancashire, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a Lancashire city in north-west England, an example of a city.

clue.text: Fees set for law sittings

definitions.meaning: rates of payment, as in agreed charges
periods during which the law courts sit

explanation.surface: Charges fixed for court sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the law courts sit in named periods such as Michaelmas and Hilary.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms are agreed rates of charging, and the sessions in which courts sit.

clue.text: Gin? Some coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means the word for some is read from bottom to top

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Is a bit of gin on its way?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink but is a snare for catching animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare or trap for catching game.

clue.text: Go to prison for bad verse and metre

indicators.note: and joins the second piece after the first
bad verse is poetry gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: time is musical metre, as in three-four time

explanation.surface: A poet jailed for writing awful poetry with faulty rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve time is the idiom for spending a sentence in jail.

clue.text: Still quits

definitions.meaning: used for emphasis, as in still more or yet more
having settled a debt so that no one owes anything

explanation.definitionFit: Even intensifies a comparison like still, and two people square with each other are quits.

clue.text: Noble brew of ale that's about right

indicators.note: about means the stirred letters go round the abbreviation for right
a brew is something mixed up, so the letters of ale are stirred

explanation.surface: An aristocrat whose beer is just right.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: With this gadget, I can mix in fruit

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

indicators.note: mix means the letters of I can are blended together

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that this kitchen gadget lets them blend fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I can mix' reads as a boast, but 'mix' is the signal to rearrange the words 'I can', which then go 'in' the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine for a household job, a gadget.

clue.text: Agree to differ, being passionate

indicators.note: to differ means the letters of agree end up different in order

explanation.surface: Two people agreeing to differ, while still feeling strongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agree to differ' reads as an idiom, but it means rearrange the letters of agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and enthusiastic, close to passionate.
